hBbso9LXNcg: Half life is the time when the drug is taken again like amoxicillin q12h means half life 12 hours

Half-life and dosing interval are different. Amoxicillin prescribed every 12 hours does not have a 12-hour half-life; the cited label reports about 61 minutes. The dosing interval also depends on pharmacodynamics, formulation and clinical context.

Determination of drug dose taken by pt. who is unconscious if the timing when dose was taken is known , there is another way to identify the dose taken by unconscious patient from volume of distribution

In a suitable pharmacokinetic model, a measured concentration and known timing may support an exposure estimate. Half-life alone cannot establish an ingested dose in an unconscious patient; absorption, distribution and changing elimination make overdose estimates uncertain.
elimination doesn’t depend on saturable enzyme system
First-order behavior applies where elimination is proportional to concentration, including enzyme-mediated pathways operating below saturation.
you can expect plasma concentration at any time and drug is eliminated after the fifth half life
A specified first-order model predicts concentration over time. After five half-lives, 3.125% remains; elimination is not literally complete.
drug accumulation is not common
Repeated dosing can produce accumulation with first-order kinetics; its extent depends on half-life and dosing interval.
we reach Css after 5 half lives
Under linear kinetics, a constant infusion reaches about 96.9% of its eventual steady-state concentration after five half-lives.
if we change the dose , the new Css reached after 5 half lives
After a change in maintenance input, about 4–5 half-lives are needed to approach the new steady pattern under linear kinetics.
If dosing stops, complete elimination of the drug from plasma occurs after 5 half lives
After dosing stops, five half-lives remove about 96.9% under the simple first-order model; a residual amount remains.
Css is 1.5 the dose you give
For a constant IV infusion under linear kinetics, Css = infusion rate / clearance. Dose and concentration have different units, so Css cannot be universally defined as 1.5 times a dose.
you can reach the Css with 1 half life and that is by using the loading dose
A loading dose can achieve a target concentration promptly. It does not change the intrinsic half-life or imply that steady state always occurs after one half-life.
We can reach the Css with 1 half life instead of 5 and that is by using the loading dose
A loading dose supplies an initial amount selected for a target concentration; maintenance dosing replaces subsequent elimination. There is no universal one-half-life rule.
Loading dose is needed in serious infections or arrhythmias (Emergency conditions)
Some drug regimens use loading doses when a target exposure is needed promptly, including selected anti-infective or antiarrhythmic treatments. The need and dose are medicine-specific.
Kidney is the primary organ of drug elimination
Kidneys and liver are major elimination organs; their relative contribution depends on the drug.
Drugs that conjugated in the liver are excreted through bile and into feces
Some hepatic conjugates are excreted in bile and feces; others undergo renal excretion. The route depends on the metabolite and transport mechanisms.
avoid injury of diseased organ by avoiding drugs that are cleared by that organ. Solved by giving drugs that cleared by another organ, if there is no alternatives then dose adjustment is the solution

Organ impairment can reduce elimination and increase exposure. Adjust the regimen, monitoring or medicine as indicated by drug-specific guidance. Clearance through an organ does not itself imply toxicity to that organ.
CL=0.7 *Vd/t1/2 , through this formula you can identify the half life and subsequently the dose of the drug you should give if you know clearance of that drug thus avoiding accumulation.
In a simple linear model, CL = 0.693 × Vd / t½. Clearance alone does not determine a safe dose: the target exposure, bioavailability, distribution and clinical setting also matter.
if drug cleared by certain organ , you can make it a targeted therapy to that organ. E.g. in UTI we use antibiotics that are cleared by the kidney like nitrofurantoin

Drug concentration at an infection site matters, but excretion through an organ does not establish tissue efficacy. Nitrofurantoin may treat suitable lower UTIs; it is not indicated for pyelonephritis or perinephric abscess.
weak bases may be increased by acidification of the urine
Although pH affects weak-base ionization, urinary acidification should not be generalized as routine poisoning treatment. Enhanced elimination requires substance-specific specialist guidance.
Differentiation between drug resistance and patient non compliance (if drug level is low means non compliance, if normal dose it is resistance)

A low level may reflect timing, absorption, interactions, clearance or missed doses. A level within the reference range with poor response does not by itself prove resistance. Interpret measurements with the history and clinical findings.
calculating the effect of the drug like in warfarin (anticoagulant) we calculate INR of the blood (level of coagulation of blood: the usual number Is 1.2 and when giving warfarin it increases )
Measuring a pharmacodynamic effect: INR monitors the anticoagulant effect of warfarin. It is not a warfarin concentration, and the target INR depends on the indication.
